title: bug: `moe-daemon doctor` probes /health and TCP only on 127.0.0.1 and ignores daemon.json bindHost, so a healthy daemon bound to ::1 or a LAN address gets a false [FAIL] and doctor exits 1
description:
Held-back finding (a) from defect hunt #6 (task-cea8fa39, architect-1dd28c7c, msg-0f965eaf). The governor re-checked the citations at moe/work-2026-10-24 6d6bdc51 at 17:35Z on 2026-11-03.

PROBLEM:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.ts dials the live daemon only on a hard-coded loopback: the /health request uses `hostname: '127.0.0.1'` (:139), and the TCP fallback calls probeTcp('127.0.0.1', port, ...) (:197). Every pass/fail message names 127.0.0.1 (:183-204).
- The daemon itself records a non-loopback bind as `bindHost` in .moe/daemon.json, and its own probes map it to a reachable address: probeHostFor(bindHost) in packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:82, used at :91 and :837.
- So for a daemon started with `--host ::1` or a LAN address (MOE_BIND_HOST), doctor reports `nothing reachable on 127.0.0.1:<port>` or a TCP-only warning while the daemon is healthy, and exits 1 on that false [FAIL].
- Repro (architect-1dd28c7c, HEAD 19d5e67a, a snapshot outside the checkout): /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-cea8/A/doctor.bindhost.repro.test.ts, with output in doctor-bindhost-vitest.txt and doctor-bindhost-repro.txt next to it.

WHY BACKLOG WITH dependsOn task-88673297: the natural fix moves probeHostFor and its helpers out of index.ts into a shared module that doctor.ts imports. index.ts is held by task-88673297 (start/_run lock-failure exit code). The governor promotes this row when 88673297 is DONE.

FIX DIRECTION (the planner decides): have doctor read daemon.json bindHost and probe the same address the daemon's own readiness probe uses (probeHostFor), defaulting to 127.0.0.1 when bindHost is absent. Put the address in the messages. Add a vitest that binds a fake /health on a non-127.0.0.1 loopback address and expects pass. Narrow row: run the doctor tests plus the new test, with no full suite (epic-be924fb8 isEpicFinal is the max-order fallback; ruling msg-bbf4f109).
definitionOfDone: doctor's live-daemon probe (/health and the TCP fallback) dials the address derived from daemon.json bindHost by the same mapping the daemon's own readiness probe uses, and 127.0.0.1 when bindHost is absent. Its messages name the address it dialed.

A vitest in packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/ starts a fake healthy /health on a non-127.0.0.1 address recorded as bindHost in daemon.json. It fails on 6d6bdc51 (RED evidence in a task comment) and passes with the fix. The existing doctor tests stay green.
No behavior change for a daemon.json without bindHost: the existing doctor.test.ts cases pass unchanged.

- B1 (it.each, 2 rows): a healthy fake /health listening on ::1. daemon.json bindHost is '::1' in one row, and in the other a name that a vi.spyOn(dns.promises, 'lookup') mock resolves to ::1. The 'daemon health reachability' line matches ^[OK] and names [::1]:<port>, and exitCode is 0.

Probe IPv6 loopback once with a top-level await (listen(0, '::1') on a throwaway net server) and put it.skipIf(!HAS_V6_LOOPBACK) on B1 and B2 (it.skipIf(...).each works in vitest 5). Then run checkRef RED verbatim. Post its output with moe.add_comment as a task comment: the x/check lines, 'Tests 6 failed | 3 passed (9)' and 'RED rows failed on 6d6bdc51: 6'. implementationPlan.description:
Make doctor dial what the daemon's own daemon.json probes dial, in packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.ts.
(1) Import { healthProbeAddress, isLocalAddress, recordedProbeHost } from '../server/probeHost.js'.
(2) In probeDaemonJson, add bindHost?: string to the parsed type. It is unchecked JSON like port, and healthProbeAddress gives null for a non-string. Add the same field to DaemonJsonProbe and return parsed.bindHost on the alive pass path.
(3) probeHealth becomes probeHealth(host, port, timeoutMs) and uses hostname: host.
(4) In probeDaemonReachability, before any dial, compute const host = await healthProbeAddress(recordedProbeHost({ bindHost }), HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS), the same sequence as index.ts validateDaemonInfoForProject.
Error handling: both failures below return before any http or TCP dial. task-d6ebe4ab: daemon.json is repository content, and a /health answer from another host could name any pid.
- host === null gives { symbol: 'fail', message: `daemon.json bindHost ${shown} gave no IP address to dial (not a string, or its lookup failed or took over ${HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS}ms); not dialed` }.
- !isLocalAddress(host) gives { symbol: 'fail', message: `daemon.json bindHost ${shown} resolves to ${host}, which is not an address of this machine; not dialed` }.
Here shown = String(JSON.stringify(bindHost)).slice(0, 120). JSON escapes control characters, so repository bytes never reach the terminal raw, and the length stays bounded.
(5) const where = net.isIPv6(host) ? `[${host}]:${port}` : `${host}:${port}`. Call probeHealth(host, ...) and probeTcp(host, ...), so the TCP fallback dials the same address. The six existing reachability messages say ${where} where they said 127.0.0.1:${port}.
With bindHost absent, recordedProbeHost gives 127.0.0.1, so the dial and every message stay byte-identical (DoD 3). Do not add a foreign (WSL-boundary) daemon.json path: doctor has none today, and this row adds none. A verified reference is the prototype /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-576e/tree/packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.ts, about 25 changed lines.

Adversarial self-review of this task's own diff (adversarial-self-review skill), as the last step. Check each of these:
(a) The move is pure. --color-moved shows the five definitions unchanged except the export keywords and the Pick<> parameter. index.ts has no other hunk except imports, and nothing still references a deleted local.
(b) No path dials a bindHost that yields no literal or a non-local one. Both FAILs return before probeHealth and probeTcp; B4 and B5 prove it with the http.request spy.
(c) Without bindHost, the dial is 127.0.0.1 and every message is unchanged.
(d) A zoned literal (fe80::1%eth0) is not local, so it FAILs without a dial, as in the daemon.
(e) Messages put IPv6 addresses in brackets.
(f) The worst case adds one 2 s lookup to the existing 2 s /health and 2 s TCP bounds.
(g) doctor is a one-shot CLI and the helpers are stateless, so there is no concurrency hazard.
(h) The shown bindHost is JSON-escaped and capped.
(i) No added line contains a project.json globalRails.forbiddenPatterns string.
(j) The RED comment is posted on the task.
Fix anything you find, then re-run GREEN, so the verification test output you submit is fresh.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: `moe-daemon doctor`'s daemon health reachability probe (GET /health and its TCP fallback) dials the address the daemon's own daemon.json probes dial. That address is healthProbeAddress(recordedProbeHost({ bindHost })), and it is dialed only when isLocalAddress holds for it. Without a bindHost, or for a 0.0.0.0, :: or wsl bind, that address is 127.0.0.1, as today. Every reachability message names the dialed address, with IPv6 in brackets ([::1]:<port>). A bindHost that yields no IP literal (not a string, or its lookup fails or times out), or that names another machine, fails the probe with exit 1, and nothing is dialed. The helpers move unchanged from index.ts to server/probeHost.ts, so the daemon lifecycle and doctor share one rule.
acceptanceCriteria: B1: a healthy fake /health on ::1, with daemon.json bindHost '::1' or with a name resolving to ::1, gives [OK] naming [::1]:<port>, exit 0.
B2: a non-HTTP listener on ::1 with bindHost '::1' gives [WARN] naming [::1]:<port>. The TCP fallback dials the bindHost address, not 127.0.0.1.
B3: bindHost 0.0.0.0, :: or wsl is probed on 127.0.0.1, and the message names 127.0.0.1:<port>.
B4: bindHost 192.0.2.10 gives [FAIL] naming it, with 'not an address of this machine' and 'not dialed'. http.request is never called, and doctor exits 1.
B5: a bindHost that does not resolve, or that is not a string, gives [FAIL] '... not dialed'. http.request is never called, and doctor exits 1.
Without bindHost in daemon.json the dial and every message are unchanged. doctor.test.ts is byte-identical to 6d6bdc51 and passes.

doctor's exit rule is unchanged: only a [FAIL] exits 1.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Copy probeHostFor into doctor.ts. Rejected: the security rule (isLocalAddress plus healthProbeAddress) would then live in two copies that can drift. (2) Have doctor.ts import from index.ts. Rejected: index.ts already imports doctor.ts, so that is a cycle, and it pulls the whole daemon into doctor. (3) Fold the helpers into server/bindHosts.ts. Workable, but that file is the listener side and would need dns and logger; a dedicated server/probeHost.ts keeps the move pure. (4) Dial bindHost directly, without the isLocalAddress guard. Rejected: it would reopen task-d6ebe4ab for doctor, since a /health answer from another host could claim any pid. No docs change: no doc names doctor's probe address, and TROUBLESHOOTING's 'bindHost not local' entry already explains the rule. docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md is also queued for task-57fe7ad1.
